gpt.rationale: For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may terminate a residential tenancy by giving the tenant actual notice specifying a termination date at least 14 days after the tenant receives the notice. federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.

machine_verified_cases.holding_summary: In a retaliatory eviction claim the tenant need not prove retaliation was the landlord's sole motivation; tenant must show retaliatory motive was a substantial or motivating factor, whereupon the burden shifts to the landlord to prove the same decision would have been made absent the retaliatory motive.
machine_verified_cases.controlling_quote: We hold that the burden of proof in a retaliatory eviction case under 9 V.S.A. § 4465 should be allocated as follows. The tenant has the initial burden of proving that a protected activity was a substantial or motivating factor in the landlord's decision to evict. If the tenant meets this burden, the landlord has the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that he would have made the same decision even if the tenant had not engaged in the protected activity.
